sequence.name: The Island
sequence.text:
1
The Island
10 MINUTES
Instructions

NOTE: The Island is a spreadsheet you make yourself with one column called Island and another column called Canoed Away.

If a question is still mystifying after Camo, just add the citation of the question to the Island.

This means at least one of these three things is true:

I don't understand why the right answer is right.

I don't understand why the wrong answer is wrong.

I have no idea how I could get this right in the future.

At the start of prep each day, spend 5 minutes on the Island retrying a question or two. 

If the question clicks, move it to Canoed Away. Otherwise, keep it on the Island. 

Fill in your Wrong Answer Journal with the new information you've learned now that the question has canoed away.

Click here to go to The Island (scroll to the bottom!)

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Translation + CLIR Drill
sequence.text:
2
Translation + CLIR Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Start a stopwatch.

Read and translate the stimulus* out loud in chunks.

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue this process on every stimulus chunk until you reach the end of stimulus.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Stop the stopwatch and record your time.

sequence.name: Mixed Timing Marathon
sequence.text:
3
Mixed Timing Marathon
8 SECTIONS
Instructions

Complete six to eight LR sections* in one sitting with no breaks, or complete six to eight RC sections in one sitting with no breaks.

Alternate test-day timed sections with Marathon-timed sections throughout the Marathon.

This means, on the first section of the Marathon, you will move on to the next section immediately once your LawHub section timer expires (no extra time).

On the next section, you will follow the Marathon timing procedures noted in the Marathon instructions.

You can choose to alternate the test-day timed sections and Marathon-timed sections in any pattern you want.

For instance, it may be useful to alternate every two sections of test-day timing with one section of Marathon timing (2:1:2:1:2).

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Camo Review
sequence.text:
4
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
5
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click here to go to your Wrong Answer Journal

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

The purpose of Mixed Timing Marathon Routines is to gradually integrate test-day timing standards into your skillset while minimally disrupting accuracy.

By allowing alternation between Marathon timing and test-day timing, you have the opportunity to reaffirm your standards without compromise during the Marathon-timed sections and then get used to pushing those standards into the test-day timing window.

Don't attempt Mixed Timing Marathon Routines if your marathon-timed sections are 10+ minutes from test-day timing.

Mixed Timing Marathons are not typically as effective as regular Marathons at large time reduction (10+ minutes) since the alternation makes it more difficult to reach the flow state required for subconscious skill integration (which is what allows the time to drop).

However, Mixed Timing Marathons are great to ease into how test day will feel.

How This Should Be Done

To make the most of a Mixed Timing Marathon Routine, the variation between Marathon-timed sections and test-day timed sections shouldn't be too great.

You don't want the two kinds of timed sections to feel like a yo-yo (one section with very high timing, followed by another section with very low timing).

Ideally, there isn't much of a difference between the Marathon-timed sections and the test-day timed sections. Since you are never allowed to end sections before your countdown test-day timer expires (35 minutes, 53 minutes, etc), the only time variation you should see between sections is higher times on some of the Marathon-timed sections.

Try to keep Marathon timed-sections to a maximum of 10 minutes over your test-day timed sections.

This advice shouldn't be a reason to continuously check the time during Marathon-timed sections – instead, think of this advice as a caution against jumping into this Speed Routine before you're ready.

Marathon Routine Protocols

Warm up before any Marathon-style Routine so you can hit the first section with a running start.

If you don't warm up first, the Marathon will not speed you up as much because it will take you longer to build momentum.

Always Camo + Wrong Answer Journal at the end of a Marathon Routine day to avoid building up too much Camo debt.

The normal "wait at least 24 hours before you Camo" rule does not apply to Marathons.

Never interrupt a Marathon to Camo in between sections.

Camo the Marathon sections in the order of completion.

This means you should Camo the first section of your Marathon first, the second section next, and so on.

Complete the entire Camo + Wrong Answer Journal process for each Marathon section before checking any Marathon scores and before starting the Camo process on another Marathon section. Camo and Wrong Answer Journal each section one at a time.

SHOW LESS
How to Move On

If your test-day timed sections crash and burn on the Mixed Timing Marathons, but you have hit goal time and accuracy on the Marathon-timed sections before, don't give up hope.

You may just be anxious about the countdown timer on test-day timed sections and need experience to acclimate.

Try progressing to Marathon Routines to ground yourself in your accurate, controlled process that consistently fits within test-day timed constraints without the countdown timer.

If you sometimes hit goal time and accuracy in your Mixed Timing Marathon, progress to a Test-Day Timing Marathon Routine.

If you're hitting your goal time and accuracy in the majority of your sections, take a Practice Test (PT).

If your test-day timed sections crash and burn on the Mixed Timing Marathons, but you have hit goal time and accuracy on the Marathon-timed sections before, don't give up hope.

You may just be anxious about the countdown timer on test-day timed sections and need experience to acclimate.

Try progressing to Marathon Routines to ground yourself in your accurate, controlled process that consistently fits within test-day timed constraints without the countdown timer.

If you sometimes hit goal time and accuracy in your Mixed Timing Marathon, progress to a Test-Day Timing Marathon Routine.

If you're hitting your goal time and accuracy in the majority of your sections, take a Practice Test (PT).

Mixed Timing Marathon Routine
Why Are We Doing This?

The purpose of Mixed Timing Marathon Routines is to gradually integrate test-day timing standards into your skillset while minimally disrupting accuracy.

By allowing alternation between Marathon timing and test-day timing, you have the opportunity to reaffirm your standards without compromise during the Marathon-timed sections and then get used to pushing those standards into the test-day timing window.

Don't attempt Mixed Timing Marathon Routines if your marathon-timed sections are 10+ minutes from test-day timing.

Mixed Timing Marathons are not typically as effective as regular Marathons at large time reduction (10+ minutes) since the alternation makes it more difficult to reach the flow state required for subconscious skill integration (which is what allows the time to drop).

However, Mixed Timing Marathons are great to ease into how test day will feel.

How To Pull This Off

To make the most of a Mixed Timing Marathon Routine, the variation between Marathon-timed sections and test-day timed sections shouldn't be too great.

You don't want the two kinds of timed sections to feel like a yo-yo (one section with very high timing, followed by another section with very low timing).

Ideally, there isn't much of a difference between the Marathon-timed sections and the test-day timed sections. Since you are never allowed to end sections before your countdown test-day timer expires (35 minutes, 53 minutes, etc), the only time variation you should see between sections is higher times on some of the Marathon-timed sections.

Try to keep Marathon timed-sections to a maximum of 10 minutes over your test-day timed sections.

This advice shouldn't be a reason to continuously check the time during Marathon-timed sections – instead, think of this advice as a caution against jumping into this Speed Routine before you're ready.

Marathon Routine Protocols

Warm up before any Marathon-style Routine so you can hit the first section with a running start.

If you don't warm up first, the Marathon will not speed you up as much because it will take you longer to build momentum.

Always Camo + Wrong Answer Journal at the end of a Marathon Routine day to avoid building up too much Camo debt.

The normal "wait at least 24 hours before you Camo" rule does not apply to Marathons.

Never interrupt a Marathon to Camo in between sections.

Camo the Marathon sections in the order of completion.

This means you should Camo the first section of your Marathon first, the second section next, and so on.

Complete the entire Camo + Wrong Answer Journal process for each Marathon section before checking any Marathon scores and before starting the Camo process on another Marathon section. Camo and Wrong Answer Journal each section one at a time.

How To Move On

If your test-day timed sections crash and burn on the Mixed Timing Marathons, but you have hit goal time and accuracy on the Marathon-timed sections before, don't give up hope.

You may just be anxious about the countdown timer on test-day timed sections and need experience to acclimate.

Try progressing to Marathon Routines to ground yourself in your accurate, controlled process that consistently fits within test-day timed constraints without the countdown timer.

If you sometimes hit goal time and accuracy in your Mixed Timing Marathon, progress to a Test-Day Timing Marathon Routine.

If you're hitting your goal time and accuracy in the majority of your sections, take a Practice Test (PT).
